mainTopic: How כהנים share קרבנות (no trading of shares), and which unusual offerings the כהנים receive (מנחות 73a)
overview: The amud opens in the middle of a בריתא about how the כהנים share their portions of קרבנות. Again and again it suggests a reason why a כהן might trade his share of one offering for a share of another: מנחות for עופות, עופות for זבחים, one מנחה for another, two of the very same kind, or offerings of lesser holiness (קדשים קלים). Each suggestion is rejected by another phrase from ויקרא 7:9–12, so no trading is allowed. The word איש adds that an adult כהן gets a share even with a מום, but a minor does not. The גמרא then works out which word teaches the no-trading law (the extra ו of וכל), so that the rest of the פסוק stays free for חזקיה's teaching. רבינא brings a different source from לוי's בריתא on במדבר 18:9. In that בריתא, each 'every' adds something the כהנים receive: the מצורע's oil, the עומר and the סוטה's מנחה, the bird חטאת, and the אשם נזיר. It ends by teaching that גזל הגר is the כהן's own property. The amud closes as רב הונא begins a new statement, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The verse says every meal offering is shared equally among the כהנים
steps.stepSummary: The בריתא quotes the פסוק 'every מנחה baked in the oven... shall all the sons of אהרן have, each man like his brother' to show that the כהנים share a מנחה equally.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'And every meal offering that is baked in the oven... shall all the sons of אהרן have, each man like his brother.'
steps.whatsHappening: The בריתא brings a פסוק to prove that the כהנים must split a מנחה evenly and cannot swap it for a share of an animal קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each כהן takes his equal portion from this מנחה itself. He cannot give up his share of the מנחה and take a piece of a זבח instead. The rest of the בריתא will test whether this rule really reaches every kind of trade.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The verse teaches': introduces a פסוק that settles the question
A meal offering made of flour
Oven
'Each man like his brother': an equal share for everyone

phrases.english: The verse states:
"And every meal offering that is baked in the oven
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:9–10. The בריתא joins words from both פסוקים into one quote.

phrases.english: shall all the sons of Aaron have,
each man like his brother."

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: וְכׇל הַמִּנְחָה אֲשֶׁר תֵּאָפֶה בַּתַּנּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a בריתא that started earlier, answering its suggestion that מנחות could be traded for זבחים.
steps.raayaObject: מנחות may not be traded for shares of זבחים; each מנחה is divided equally.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 7:9–10: 'לכל בני אהרן תהיה איש כאחיו'

steps.title: Maybe meal offerings can be traded for bird offerings
steps.stepSummary: The בריתא suggests that even if מנחות can't be traded for זבחים, maybe they can be traded for עופות, because a poor person brings a מנחה in place of a bird.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think: they may not trade meal offerings for animal offerings, because meal offerings never replace animal offerings for a poor person. But they may trade meal offerings for bird offerings, because meal offerings do replace bird offerings for a poor person.
steps.whatsHappening: The בריתא raises a possible exception to the rule from step 1 and sets up the next פסוק to reject it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that two kinds of קרבן that can stand in for each other are closely connected, so trading between them might be fine. A very poor person who can't afford birds brings a מנחה instead (as in a קרבן עולה ויורד). Animals never get replaced directly by a מנחה, so those two stay separate.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You might have thought': introduces a suggestion the בריתא will reject
They will take a share, here meaning trade one share for another
Animal offerings
Bird offerings
They take the place of them in poverty: a cheaper offering a poor person brings instead

steps.confusionAlert: 'יחלקו כנגד' here does not mean simply dividing a קרבן. It means a כהן gives up his share of one קרבן in exchange for a share of another.

phrases.english: One might think that they may not take a share
of meal offerings in exchange for animal offerings,
since they do not take their place in poverty,
but they may take a share
of meal offerings in exchange for bird offerings,
since they do take their place in poverty.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל לֹא יַחְלְקוּ מְנָחוֹת כְּנֶגֶד זְבָחִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts step 1 for זבחים but suggests an exception for עופות.
steps.kashyaTarget: How far the no-trading rule from step 1 reaches
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: מנחות replace עופות for a poor person, so the two are connected enough that trading between them might be allowed.

steps.title: The phrase about the deep pan rules out trading meal offerings for birds
steps.stepSummary: The בריתא answers with 'וכל נעשה במרחשת לכל בני אהרן תהיה': even the trade of מנחות for עופות is not allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'And all that is prepared in the deep pan... shall all the sons of אהרן have.'
steps.whatsHappening: The בריתא uses another phrase from the פסוק to reject the suggestion of step 2.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Repeating that the deep-pan מנחה belongs to all the sons of אהרן means each one must take his share from the מנחה itself. So the close link between מנחות and עופות still does not allow a trade.

keyTerms.meaning: A deep pan used for one type of מנחה

phrases.english: The verse states:
"And all that is prepared in the deep pan
shall all the sons of Aaron have."

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: וְכׇל נַעֲשָׂה בַּמַּרְחֶשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the exception suggested in step 2.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since מנחות replace עופות in poverty, they could be traded for them.
steps.terutzMaskana: The extra phrase teaches that מנחות may not be traded for עופות either.

steps.title: Maybe bird offerings can be traded for animal offerings
steps.stepSummary: The בריתא suggests that even if מנחות can't be traded for עופות, maybe עופות can be traded for זבחים, since both have blood put on the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think: they may not trade meal offerings for bird offerings, because birds are blood offerings and meal offerings are flour offerings. But they may trade bird offerings for animal offerings, because both are blood offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The בריתא suggests a new kind of connection, the type of material offered, and sets up the next פסוק to reject it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reasoning has changed from 'which one replaces which' to 'what are they made of.' Birds and animals both have their blood put on the מזבח, so they look like the same family, while flour is completely different.

keyTerms.meaning: Kinds of offerings whose blood is put on the מזבח
Kinds of offerings made of flour

phrases.english: One might think that they may not take a share
of meal offerings in exchange for bird offerings,
since these are types of blood offerings
and those are types of flour offerings;
but they may take a share of bird offerings in exchange for animal offerings,
since both these and those are types of blood offerings.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל לֹא יַחְלְקוּ מְנָחוֹת כְּנֶגֶד עוֹפוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts step 3's ruling and suggests a new exception based on a different kind of similarity.
steps.kashyaTarget: Whether the no-trading rule also covers עופות and זבחים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: עופות and זבחים are both blood offerings, so they are similar enough that trading might be allowed.

steps.title: The phrase about the flat pan rules out trading birds for animals
steps.stepSummary: The בריתא answers with 'ועל מחבת לכל בני אהרן תהיה': birds may not be traded for animals either.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'And on a pan... shall all the sons of אהרן have.'
steps.whatsHappening: The בריתא uses yet another phrase from the פסוק to reject the suggestion of step 4.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This phrase looks extra, so the בריתא uses it to teach something new. Being similar in material (both blood offerings) is not enough to allow a trade.

keyTerms.meaning: A flat pan used for one type of מנחה

phrases.english: The verse states:
"And on a pan
shall all the sons of Aaron have."

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: וְעַל מַחֲבַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the exception suggested in step 4.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since עופות and זבחים are both blood offerings, they could be traded.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even עופות may not be traded for זבחים.

steps.title: Maybe one meal offering can be traded for another
steps.stepSummary: The בריתא suggests that even if עופות can't be traded for זבחים, maybe one מנחה can be traded for another, since all מנחות are prepared by hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think: they may not trade bird offerings for animal offerings, because birds are prepared by hand and animals are prepared with a utensil. But they may trade one meal offering for another, because both are prepared by hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The בריתא suggests another exception, trading within the same category, and sets up the next phrase of the פסוק to reject it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Birds are killed by hand (מליקה, pinching the neck), while animals are slaughtered with a knife, so those are different. Two מנחות are the closest pair of all, the same kind made the same way, so trading them seems most reasonable.

keyTerms.meaning: Their preparation is done by hand
With a utensil, here a slaughtering knife

phrases.english: One might think that they may not take a share
of bird offerings in exchange for animal offerings,
since these are processed by hand,
phrases.notes: Birds are killed by pinching the neck by hand, not with a knife.

phrases.english: and those are processed with a utensil;
but they may take a share
of meal offerings in exchange for meal offerings,
since both these and those are processed by hand.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל לֹא יַחְלְקוּ עוֹפוֹת כְּנֶגֶד זְבָחִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts step 5's ruling and suggests the closest possible exception: trading מנחה for מנחה.
steps.kashyaTarget: Whether the no-trading rule applies even within the same category of מנחות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: All מנחות are prepared by hand, so they are alike enough to be traded.

steps.title: Even one meal offering may not be traded for another
steps.stepSummary: The בריתא answers with 'וכל מנחה בלולה בשמן... לכל בני אהרן תהיה': even trading one מנחה for another is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'And every meal offering mixed with oil... shall all the sons of אהרן have.'
steps.whatsHappening: The בריתא uses another phrase from the פסוק to reject trading one מנחה for another.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every suggested link so far (replacing in poverty, both blood offerings, both made by hand) has been rejected by a separate phrase. Even two מנחות may not be traded. The בריתא will still test closer cases next: מנחות of the very same kind (step 8) and קדשים קלים (step 10).

keyTerms.meaning: Mixed with oil, describing a type of מנחה

steps.whatToRemember: Step by step, the בריתא rules out every kind of trade: מנחות for זבחים, מנחות for עופות, עופות for זבחים, and even מנחה for מנחה. Each כהן must get an equal share of each קרבן itself.

phrases.english: The verse states:
"And every meal offering mixed with oil...
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:10

phrases.english: shall all the sons of Aaron have."

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: וְכׇל מִנְחָה בְלוּלָה בַשֶּׁמֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion of step 6; the ברייתא then continues with a narrower suggestion in step 8.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Even two מנחות may not be traded for one another.

steps.title: Maybe the same kind of pan offering can be traded
steps.stepSummary: The בריתא suggests that even if a מחבת offering can't be traded for a מרחשת offering, maybe two offerings of the same kind can be traded.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think that a pan-offering can't be traded for a deep-pan offering, since one comes out hard and the other soft. But maybe a pan-offering can be traded for another pan-offering, and a deep-pan offering for another deep-pan offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The בריתא makes one more 'you might think' suggestion. It is setting up the next פסוק to knock it down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מחבת makes a hard product and a מרחשת makes a soft one, so trading between them looks unfair. But two מחבת offerings are exactly alike, so trading them seems harmless. That is the new suggestion.

keyTerms.meaning: A flat pan; a מנחה fried on it comes out hard
A deep pan; a מנחה made in it comes out soft
Take a share in exchange for (trade one share for another)
Its making produces something hard / soft

phrases.english: One might think they may not trade shares
of a pan-offering in exchange for a deep-pan offering,
or of a deep-pan offering in exchange for a pan-offering,
since the making of this one turns out hard
and the making of that one turns out soft,
but they may trade a pan-offering for a pan-offering
and a deep-pan offering for a deep-pan offering

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל לֹא יַחְלְקוּ מַחֲבַת כְּנֶגֶד מַרְחֶשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the case further: after trading between different מנחות was forbidden, it suggests that trading identical kinds might still be allowed.
steps.kashyaTarget: How far the no-trading rule reaches
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Identical offerings have no difference in value, so trading them seems harmless.

steps.title: Even the same kind may not be traded
steps.stepSummary: The word וחרבה teaches that even two identical offerings may not be traded.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק teaches: 'Or dry, shall all the sons of אהרן have.'
steps.whatsHappening: The בריתא uses the next words of the פסוק to reject the suggestion from Step 8.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says each offering belongs to all the sons of אהרן. So even two identical offerings may not be traded, and every כהן takes his part of each one.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Or dry', a מנחה without oil
The פסוק teaches (introduces the source that settles the question)

phrases.english: Therefore the verse teaches:
"Or dry, shall all the sons of Aaron have."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:10

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: וַחֲרֵבָה לְכׇל בְּנֵי אַהֲרֹן תִּהְיֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 8's suggestion with a פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Derivation from a word in the פסוק
steps.terutzMaskana: No trading at all, even between identical offerings.

steps.title: Maybe trading is allowed with lesser-holiness offerings
steps.stepSummary: The בריתא suggests that the no-trading rule may apply only to קדשי קדשים, not to קדשים קלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think they may not trade shares of the most holy offerings, but may trade shares of offerings of lesser holiness.
steps.whatsHappening: The בריתא asks whether the whole no-trading rule also covers a different level of holiness. It is setting up the next proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everything taught so far was about מנחות, which are קדשי קדשים. The new suggestion is that offerings of lower holiness, like a תודה, might be treated more loosely.

keyTerms.meaning: Offerings of the highest holiness (like מנחות)
Offerings of lesser holiness (like a תודה or שלמים)

phrases.english: One might think they may not trade shares in the most holy offerings,
but they may trade shares in offerings of lesser holiness

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל לֹא יַחְלְקוּ בְּקׇדְשֵׁי קָדָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from types of מנחות to a new question about a different level of holiness.
steps.kashyaTarget: Whether the no-trading rule applies to קדשים קלים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Lesser holiness might mean stricter rules don't apply.

steps.title: Lesser-holiness offerings follow the same rule
steps.stepSummary: From איש כאחיו next to the פסוק about a תודה, the בריתא learns that trading is forbidden in קדשים קלים too.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק teaches: 'one like his brother,' and right after it: 'If for a thanks offering.' Just as they don't trade in the most holy offerings, so they don't trade in offerings of lesser holiness.
steps.whatsHappening: The בריתא answers Step 10 by linking two neighboring פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: איש כאחיו ends the פסוק about מנחות (ויקרא 7:10), and close by, in 7:12, the תורה discusses the תודה, which is a קדשים קלים offering. Because the two are near each other, the rule from the מנחות carries over to the תודה. So קדשים קלים may not be traded either.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Each man like his brother', meaning equal shares
Thanks offering, one of the קדשים קלים
Just as ... so too (sets up a comparison)

phrases.english: Therefore the verse teaches: "one like his brother,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:10

phrases.english: and next to it: "If for a thanks offering"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:12, the next topic in the פסוקים, which is a lesser-holiness offering.

phrases.english: just as they do not trade shares in the most holy offerings,
so too they do not trade shares in offerings of lesser holiness.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: אִישׁ כְּאָחִיו, וְאִם עַל תּוֹדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects Step 10's suggestion using the closeness of two פסוקים.
steps.terutzMaskana: Trading is forbidden in קדשים קלים as well.
steps.whatToRemember: No trading of shares at all: not between different offerings, not between identical ones, and not in קדשים קלים.

steps.title: Who receives a share: adult yes, minor no
steps.stepSummary: The word איש teaches that an adult כהן receives a share even with a מום, but a קטן does not, even without one.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'A man': a grown man takes a share, even if he has a blemish. But a minor does not take a share, even if he has no blemish.
steps.whatsHappening: The בריתא learns a new rule from the word איש: who is included in the sharing at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here חולק means 'receives a share', not 'trades'. Being an adult is what counts, not being fit to serve. A blemished adult still eats, while an unblemished child does not.

keyTerms.meaning: A כהן with a physical blemish that bars him from serving
A minor, under bar מצוה age
Unblemished, physically whole
Here: receives a share

steps.confusionAlert: Until now יחלקו and חולקין meant trading one share for another. In this line חולק simply means getting a portion.

phrases.english: "A man" teaches:
a grown man receives a share, even if he has a blemish,
but a minor does not receive a share, even if he is unblemished.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִישׁ – אִישׁ חוֹלֵק, וַאֲפִילּוּ בַּעַל מוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same פסוק to teach a separate rule about who gets a share.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Adult כהנים share even with a מום; minors do not share even without one.

steps.title: The no-trading law comes from the word כל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the no-trading law is learned only from the word כל, which leaves the rest of the פסוק free for חזקיה's teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: That law comes from the word 'every'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers an unspoken question. If this בריתא uses the פסוק for the no-trading law, how could חזקיה use the same פסוק for a different teaching?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer is that the no-trading law comes from only one word, כל. The rest of the פסוק is still available for what חזקיה learned from it.

keyTerms.meaning: It comes out from (is learned from)
'Every', a word in the פסוק used as a source

phrases.english: That law is learned from the word "every",
phrases.notes: The גמרא means: the no-trading law needs only this one word, so חזקיה can still learn his teaching from the rest of the פסוק.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא מִכׇּל נָפְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Steps back from the בריתא to reconcile it with חזקיה's use of the same פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the פסוק into separate sources
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The whole פסוק is used for the no-trading law, which leaves nothing for חזקיה.

steps.title: But כל was already used for רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the word כל was already used for the teaching of רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't you already use that word for the teaching of רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges Step 13. The word כל is already taken.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word normally teaches only one thing. Since כל was already used to teach that a baked מנחה must be all one type, it can't also be the source for the no-trading law.

keyTerms.meaning: You already took it out (used it) for another teaching

phrases.english: But haven't you already used it
for the teaching of Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda?
phrases.notes: This is his teaching from earlier (63b): a baked מנחה must be all loaves or all wafers, not a mix.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אַפֵּיקְתֵּיהּ לְכִדְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the source proposed in Step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: Using כל as the source for no-trading
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word is already used for a different teaching, so it can't teach this too.

steps.title: The source is the extra ו in וכל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the no-trading law comes from the extra ו, 'and', in וכל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, that law comes from 'and every'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new source that isn't already taken: the added letter ו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: כל itself goes to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, and the extra ו in וכל teaches the no-trading law. The rest of the פסוק stays free for חזקיה, so every teaching has its own source.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (drops the earlier answer for a new one)
'And every', where the extra ו is expounded

steps.whatToRemember: The no-trading law comes from the ו of וכל. כל teaches רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's rule, and חזקיה learns his teaching from the rest of the פסוק.

phrases.english: Rather, that law is learned from "and every".

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, הָהוּא מִוְכׇל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected source from Step 13 with a new one.
steps.terutzMaskana: The source is the extra ו of וכל.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Each teaching has its own source in the פסוק: ו for no-trading, כל for רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, and the rest of the פסוק for חזקיה.

steps.title: רבינא brings a different source from Levi's teaching
steps.stepSummary: רבינא says the law that the עומר and the מנחת קנאות are eaten comes from a ברייתא of לוי on the פסוק 'every offering of theirs, every meal offering of theirs...'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: It comes from what לוי teaches. As לוי teaches: 'Every offering of theirs, and every meal offering of theirs, and every sin offering of theirs, and every guilt offering of theirs.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא offers a new source for the same law, different from the earlier derivations. He quotes the פסוק that לוי's ברייתא explains, setting up the line-by-line reading that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the גמרא was working with other words of the תורה to find the source. רבינא moves to a different פסוק, in במדבר 18:9, about the gifts given to the כהנים. Each repeated 'every' (כל) in that פסוק will be read as adding something extra.

keyTerms.meaning: It comes from (the source is)
Every / for all. Each one here will be read as adding something
Their meal offerings

steps.title: Every offering adds the leper's log of oil
steps.stepSummary: 'Every offering of theirs' teaches that the כהנים eat the לוג שמן of a מצורע, even though the פסוק says 'from the fire'.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Every offering of theirs' comes to include the לוג of oil of a מצורע. You might have thought that since the תורה wrote 'from the fire', this oil is left out. So the פסוק teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains the first phrase, 'every offering', and says it adds the מצורע's oil to the gifts the כהנים eat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same פסוק says the gifts are 'from the fire', which sounds like it covers only things that go on the מזבח. The מצורע's oil never goes on the fire, so we might have left it out. The extra word כל includes it anyway.

steps.title: Every meal offering adds the omer and the sotah's offering
steps.stepSummary: 'Every meal offering of theirs' teaches that the מנחת העומר and the מנחת קנאות are eaten, even though neither one brings atonement.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Every meal offering of theirs' comes to include the מנחת העומר and the מנחת קנאות. You might have thought that since the תורה said 'They shall eat those through which atonement was made', these two are left out. The עומר comes to permit the new grain, and the other one comes to clarify whether the woman sinned. So the פסוק teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the part רבינא needs: 'every meal offering' adds the עומר and the סוטה's מנחה to what the כהנים eat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פסוק in שמות says the כהנים eat offerings 'through which atonement was made'. The עומר does not bring כפרה; it makes the new grain permitted. The סוטה's offering does not bring כפרה either; it helps find out the truth. The extra כל includes both anyway.

keyTerms.meaning: The barley offering brought on the second day of פסח
The meal offering of jealousy brought by a סוטה
Through which atonement was made
To permit (here, the new grain)
To clarify (whether the woman sinned)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the actual answer to the question רבינא was addressing: it gives a direct source that these two מנחות are eaten by the כהנים.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מנחת העומר and the מנחת קנאות are eaten by the כהנים, even though they do not bring atonement.

steps.title: Every sin offering adds the bird sin offering
steps.stepSummary: 'Every sin offering of theirs' teaches that the כהנים eat the חטאת העוף, even though it is not slaughtered and might seem like a נבילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Every sin offering of theirs' comes to include the bird sin offering. You might have thought it is a נבילה. So the פסוק teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains the third phrase, 'every sin offering', and says it adds the bird חטאת to what the כהנים eat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A bird חטאת is killed by מליקה, pinching the neck, not by שחיטה. Normally an animal killed without שחיטה is a נבילה and may not be eaten. The extra כל teaches that this חטאת is still eaten by the כהנים.

keyTerms.meaning: A sin offering brought from a bird
An animal that died without proper שחיטה, forbidden to eat
Killing a bird offering by pinching the back of its neck

steps.whatToRemember: In לוי's ברייתא, each 'every' (כל) in במדבר 18:9 adds an item the כהנים eat: the מצורע's oil, the עומר and the סוטה's מנחה, and the bird חטאת. Each one answers a reason we might have left it out.

phrases.english: "And every sin offering of theirs":
to include the bird sin offering,
it might enter your mind to say:

phrases.notes: The bird is killed by pinching its neck, not by regular שחיטה, so it looks like a נבילה.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חטאת העוף is eaten by the כהנים despite being killed by מליקה.

steps.title: 'Every guilt offering of theirs' includes the nazirite's and the leper's guilt offerings
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says the words 'every guilt offering of theirs' come to include the אשם נזיר and the אשם מצורע, which the כהנים eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Every guilt offering of theirs' comes to include the guilt offering of a nazirite and the guilt offering of a leper.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves to the next phrase of the פסוק and says it includes two specific guilt offerings: the אשם נזיר and the אשם מצורע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This continues the same pattern as the earlier phrases. Each 'every...' in the פסוק comes to include a case we might have thought the כהנים do not eat. Here, the cases are two unusual guilt offerings.

The guilt offering a healed מצורע brings
To include (an extra case from a word in the פסוק)

steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Every guilt offering of theirs' includes the אשם נזיר and the אשם מצורע as eaten by the כהנים.

steps.title: The leper's guilt offering already has an explicit verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the אשם מצורע does not need this phrase, because a different פסוק already says outright that it belongs to the כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: The leper's guilt offering? It is written explicitly about it: 'For like the sin offering, the guilt offering belongs to the כהן'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא, asking why it needs a phrase to include the אשם מצורע when the תורה already states this plainly elsewhere.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A word of the פסוק should not be used to teach something we already know from another פסוק. Since ויקרא already says the אשם מצורע goes to the כהן, the ברייתא's reading seems to waste the phrase.

keyTerms.meaning: Explicitly, openly
It is written (in the תורה)

phrases.english: The guilt offering of a leper?
It is explicitly written about it:
"For like the sin offering, the guilt offering
belongs to the priest"!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 14:13

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲשַׁם מְצוֹרָע בְּהֶדְיָא כְּתִיב בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the second half of the ברייתא's reading in step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that 'every guilt offering of theirs' is needed to include the אשם מצורע.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The אשם מצורע is already explicitly given to the כהן in ויקרא 14:13, so the phrase would be unnecessary for it.

steps.title: The verse includes the nazirite's guilt offering, making it like the leper's
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the phrase is really about the אשם נזיר: it is treated like the אשם מצורע. Otherwise we might think it only 'prepares' the נזיר and is not eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it comes to include the nazirite's guilt offering, to make it like the leper's guilt offering. You might have thought it comes only to make him fit to restart, so the verse teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא changes how it reads the ברייתא. The phrase is not teaching about the אשם מצורע at all. It compares the אשם נזיר to the אשם מצורע so that the כהנים eat it too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The אשם נזיר does not atone for a sin. It only makes the נזיר ready to start his נזירות over again, so we might have thought it is not eaten. The phrase teaches that it is eaten just like the אשם מצורע, which also has a 'preparing' role.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have thought (the mistaken first idea)
To make fit or ready (not to atone)
It teaches us (otherwise)

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא still mentions the אשם מצורע, but only as the model being compared to. The new teaching is about the אשם נזיר alone.

phrases.english: Rather, it is to include the guilt offering of a nazirite

it comes to make him fit,

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְרַבּוֹת אֲשַׁם נָזִיר כַּאֲשַׁם מְצוֹרָע

steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the אשם נזיר only prepares the נזיר and does not atone, the כהנים would not eat it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The אשם נזיר is like the אשם מצורע and is eaten by the כהנים.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that an offering brought to 'prepare' someone, rather than to atone, can still be a fully eaten קרבן, just like the מנחת העומר in step 18.

steps.title: 'Which they may restore' is a stolen item from a convert, fully the כהנים' property
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says 'which they may restore' refers to גזל הגר, and 'yours and your sons'' means it is the כהן's private property, so he may even use it to marry a woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Which they may restore' is the item stolen from a convert. 'It is for you and your sons' means it is yours and your sons', even to betroth a woman with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends by explaining the last part of the פסוק: גזל הגר goes to the כהנים, and it belongs to them as personal property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a convert who has no heirs dies, money stolen from him is paid to the כהנים. The words 'yours and your sons'' teach that this is the כהן's own money, not Temple property, so he can use it for anything, even קידושין.

keyTerms.meaning: An item stolen from a convert who died without heirs; it is paid to the כהנים
To betroth (marry) a woman with it
'Which they may restore' (return)
